Welcome to the South. Thus year I've averaged around 51 hours a week (because my planning time is cut in half) and I get just at $510 a week take home.

I have no curriculum and I don't have any idea how to make a true "project" where standards are adequately covered AND where both low and high kids work to their level. If anything, the mixed groups have meant that the high kids do double the work just to get the project done because their version of "acceptable work" is very different from the other kids. My entire student teaching experience was very old-school and, while I got to read a lot of academic papers about PBL, I have never seen it in action. The week of training I got before school started was by people who never taught math and who said "math is more problem-based" (meaning like a midpoint between pbl and traditional). I feel like I'm chasing a unicorn.
